answer: Use 'clear [-f] topology [target=]<value>' in Operational Mode. It manually removes existing topology neighbor information. The target is an instance-identifier and may be: an lldp-neighbor instance (discovered via LLDP), a carrier-neighbor instance (discovered via ICMP), or an lldp-port-statistics instance (details associated with an LLDP enabled port). The -f flag forces the command without confirmation. Tip: type 'clear topology <tab>' to list the valid topology objects. Example: clear topology lldp-neighbor-ethernet-1-4-T1-1. The companion 'show topology' (Operational or Candidate Configuration mode) displays inci, links, lldp, icdp or sndp.

Run 'verify [-f] [type-select=]<value> [[target-select=]<value>] [allow-switching]' in Operational Mode. Only type-select=fiber-connection is supported. target-select is the port instance-identifier of the CableID capable card; if omitted, all paths are verified. allow-switching is boolean, default false: false verifies active paths only with no system initiated switching, true allows the CableID function to initiate switching on the OPSM so both active and inactive (working and protection) paths are covered. Precondition: equipment-policies cable-id-control must be enabled. The command prompts for confirmation (-f skips it), is non-blocking, raises the CID-verification-in-progress alarm against the NE until all queued requests finish, and returns verify-result. Check progress with show cable-id-status. Example: verify fiber-connection port-1-6-ade3 allow-switching=true.

The bert command runs in Operational Mode. Start: 'bert start test-id=TestX resource=ethernet-1-6-T1 test-signal-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-monitoring-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-direction=ingress test-signal-monitoring-direction=ingress test-duration=10'. Stop: 'bert stop test-id=TestX'; test-id is mandatory for stop. If you omit test-id on start the system generates a unique one. 100GE/400GE use scrambled-idles, ODU4 uses PRBS31 or PRBS31NONINV, CarrierCTP monitoring uses fec-frames. test-signal-direction and test-signal-monitoring-direction are ingress or egress (default none). test-duration is in seconds, minimum 10 secs, maximum up to 1000 hrs, and the default 0 means an indefinite test. Records are read with 'bert get' (by test-id, resource or AID) and removed with 'bert delete'. Multiple simultaneous BERTs can run on a facility.

You cannot create one. The cid-ptp facility is created by the system when a card supporting the CableID function is created, for example RD20TM or CAD10A, and it represents the CableID SFP and its connection to the card via the CID port. Only set and show are offered (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode): 'set cid-ptp-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>]'. managed-by reads system, and only user-created facilities can be user deleted. admin-state is not editable and the only supported value is unlock; CableID operation is not affected by the cid-ptp admin-state. The read-only 'used' attribute is true when CableID functionality is supported (default false). Example: show cid-ptp-1-4-spcid.

The eth-zr facility is the Digital Coherent 400ZR interface, auto-instantiated when the ZR TOM is provisioned; interface-type is 400ZR (Media-interface 400ZR-CFEC-DP-16QAM) and rate is fixed at 400.000 Gbit/s. fec-type is settable with default ofec; permitted values are not-applicable, cfec, ofec, noFEC, G709, i4 (EFEC-I4), i7 (EFEC-I7), sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7 and ufec7. Degrade is handled by two pairs: FEC Detected Degrade (fdd-monitoring, default disabled; fdd-threshold default 0.0195 avg BER, fdd-clear-threshold default 0.01062 avg BER) and FEC Excessive Degrade (fed-monitoring, default disabled; fed-threshold default 0.0206 avg BER, fed-clear-threshold default 0.01125 avg BER). All four thresholds are decimal64(9) in the range 0.000000001..0.1 avg BER. link-degrade-indication shows none, local-degraded, remote-degraded or local-and-remote-degraded.

The ethernet facility attribute max-packet-length sets the maximum transfer unit in octets. On 1830 GX G30 the range is 1280..18000 octets; on 1830 GX G40 the range is 1518..18000 octets. The default in both cases is 1518. Set it with 'set ethernet-<name> max-packet-length <value>' in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. Two restrictions apply: max-packet-length is configurable on card level only and applies to all interfaces on that card, and it is used only for determining the undersized/oversized packet count in 100GbE PMs.

Use 'show facilities'. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. The output is a flat list of every facility instance on the node, for example super-channel-group-1-4-L1, super-channel-1-4-L1-1, optical-carrier-1-4-L1-1, optical-channel-1-4-L1-1, trib-ptp-1-4-T11, comm-channel-1-4-L1-1, otu-1-4-L1-1-OTUCni, ethernet-1-4-T2 and odu-1-4-L1-1-ODUCni. Use the per-facility commands (for example show ethernet-<name>, show odu-<name>) to see the attributes of an individual entry.

The fc facility (set/show, Operational and Candidate Configuration mode) exposes two Fibre Channel specific attributes for the 32GFC client: tts enables or disables Transmitter Training Signal support, values enabled or disabled with default disabled; and laser-toggling-for-tts enables or disables laser toggling when tts is enabled/disabled, values enabled or disabled with default enabled. The read-only fc-type reports the signal type: FC1G, FC2G, FC4G, FC8G, FC16G or FC32G. Other settable attributes are label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), tx-mapping-mode and expected-mapping-mode (default GMP), loopback (none/facility/terminal, default none), loopback-mode, test-signal-type (default none), test-signal-direction (default ingress) and test-signal-monitoring (default false).

The flexo facility reports foic-type, a read-only attribute naming the FOICx.k interface (k parallel lanes carrying a FlexO-x interface, order x in units of 100G, per G.709.3 FlexO-LR and G.709.1 FlexO-SR). Supported values are foic1.2, foic1.4, foic2.4, foic2.8, foic3.6, foic4.8 and foic4.16, with foic4.8 the default. fec-type is also show-only, default ofec (also not-applicable, cfec, noFEC). resource-mode is the settable one: ADM selects add-drop, XC selects add-drop with regen, and the default is ADM. Example: set flexo-1-5-L1-1 resource-mode 'XC'. Also settable are label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, iid and the fdd/fed raise and clear thresholds.

Creation syntax is 'add flexo-group-<name> carriers <value> rate <value> modulation-format <value> group-id <value> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [fec-type <value>]', in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. The four mandatory arguments are carriers (string 1..32, the carriers bound to the facility), rate (the carried signal basic rate class in Gbit/s), modulation-format (not-applicable, DP-QPSK, DP-16QAM, DP-8QAM or BPSK) and group-id, an integer in the range 1..1048575 that indicates the interface group instance the FlexO-x interface belongs to and must be unique in the NE. Optional fec-type defaults to ofec; admin-state defaults to unlock and alarm-report-control to allowed.

high-speed-monitoring is a small set/show container available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode: 'set high-speed-monitoring [enabled <value>] [port <value>]' and 'show high-speed-monitoring [enabled] [port]'. It has exactly two attributes. enabled is the user configurable switch that turns high speed monitoring on or off, values true or false, default false. port is the user configurable port, a uint16 in the range 1..max, default 57500.

The interlaken facility represents the SPN2 Interlaken interface and is managed with set/show in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Its capacity is a read-only attribute fixed at 500 Gbit/s. managed-by is system only, so it is not user created or deleted. The settable attributes are label (string 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited; default allowed) and loopback (none, facility, terminal; default none, where facility tests towards the facility side and terminal towards the terminal side). Show also returns supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state and avail-state. Example: set interlaken-66-1-8 label interlaken_66_1.

On line-ptp, auto-in-service is controlled by two attributes settable on add and set. auto-in-service-enabled is the auto-in-service switch for the facility, values true or false, default false. valid-signal-time is the configurable time that represents detection of a valid signal used by the auto-in-service mechanism, a number in the range 1..7200 minutes with a default of 480. The read-only remaining-valid-signal-time (1..7200 minutes) shows the actual time left before the facility is automatically enabled by the mechanism. Both are available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, for example 'set line-ptp-1-2-1 auto-in-service-enabled true valid-signal-time 480'.

They are different objects. network-xconnect is display-only: 'show network-xconnect' takes no parameters and lists the services of the multiple user cross connections commissioned in this NE, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. nw-xconnect is the configurable networking cross-connection entity, supporting add, delete, set and show: 'add nw-xconnect-<name> endpoint1 <value> endpoint2 <value> [xcon-type <value>] [rate <value>]', 'set nw-xconnect-<name> [rate <value>]', 'show nw-xconnect-<name> [AID] [oper-state] [avail-state] [endpoint1] [endpoint2] [xcon-type] [rate]' and 'delete nw-xconnect-<name>'. Use nw-xconnect to create or change a user channel cross-connection, network-xconnect to list what is commissioned.

nw-xconnect supports four xcon-type values, and none of them joins a GCC directly to an OSC: L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 (L1-ETH to GCC0 user channel), L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0 (GCC0 to GCC0), L1-ETH-TO-OSC (L1-ETH to OSC) and L1-OSC-TO-OSC (OSC to OSC). The default is L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0. endpoint1 and endpoint2 are mandatory instance-identifiers: for L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 and L1-ETH-TO-OSC endpoint1 is a comm-eth MO of a chassis; for L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0 endpoint1 is a GCC0 comm-channel MO; for L1-OSC-TO-OSC endpoint1 is an OSCX-5 comm-channel MO. rate is the maximum user channel bandwidth, uint8 range 1..20 Mbps, default 13 for L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 and 20 for L1-ETH-TO-OSC and L1-OSC-TO-OSC. Example: add nw-xconnect-test1 xcon-type L1-ETH-TO-OSC endpoint1 comm-eth-1-16-ETH4 endpoint2 comm-channel-1-6-dwdm-line-OSCX5.

No. The high order ODU is automatically created when an SCH is created. When a CHM6 has an OTU configured on it, use 'show odu' to determine whether the ODU exists. What you create are the low order ODUs: ODU4i (100G) or ODUflexi (400G) facilities represent the low order ODUs that XCONs are mapped into, added with 'add odu-<name> odu-type <value> [parent-odu <value>] [time-slots <value>] ...'. The stated pre-condition is that the super-channel must be added before Low Order ODUs can be added. The read-only class attribute reports high-order for the top-most system-created ODUCn/ODUk, low-order (the default) for children, and mapped for a mapped client signal.

Yes. odu-diagnostics instances are keyed by direction: 'add|set|show|delete odu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction>' where direction is ingress or egress, and each direction has its own values. Per direction you can set tx-tti (hex string with 0x prefix, 1..130 characters, or printable ASCII 1..64) and expected-tti (same forms, default empty), or, in ITU style, tx-sapi/tx-dapi/tx-operator and expected-sapi/expected-dapi/expected-operator (SAPI and DAPI 1..15 ASCII or 1..32 hex, operator 1..32 ASCII or 1..66 hex). tti-style selects ITU-T-G709 (TTI split into SAPI, DAPI and OPER bytes) or proprietary (a single 64 byte string), default ITU-T-G709. Received values are read back with rx-tti, rx-tti-hex, rx-sapi, rx-dapi, rx-operator and their hex forms.

Yes, FEC is on by default. On the otu facility, fec-mode is the configured Forward Error Correction mode on the OTUk/OTUCn client, values enabled or disabled, and it defaults to enabled. fec-generation-mode, the configured FEC generation mode towards the far-end receiver, is also enabled or disabled with default enabled. fec-type defaults to ofec; the permitted values are not-applicable, cfec, ofec, G709, noFEC, i4, i7, sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7 and ufec7. All three are usable on add, set and show, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode, for example 'set otu-<name> fec-mode enabled fec-type ofec'.

Set tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting on the otu-diagnostics instance for the direction concerned. It indicates whether the TTI-Mismatch (TIM) alarm is reported or masked and, when reported, the criteria used. Permitted values are disabled (the default), full-64-bytes, SAPI, DAPI, OPER, SAPI_DAPI, SAPI_OPER, DAPI_OPER and SAPI_DAPI_OPER. To alarm only on a mismatched source trace, use SAPI: 'set otu-diagnostics-1-4-L1-1-OTUCni/ingress tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting SAPI'. direction is ingress or egress and each direction has its own values. Related attributes: tti-style (ITU-T-G709 default, or proprietary) and tim-act-enabled, which decides whether a maintenance signal is inserted per TIM, default disabled.

The stm facility reports stm-type, the type of SDH signal (STM-N), and the supported values are STM-16 and STM-64. stm-type is read-only (show). The facility name follows the Synchronous Transport Module N convention, for example N=16, 64, per ITU-T G.691. Settable attributes include label, admin-state (Lock, Unlock, Maintenance; default Unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), tx-mapping-mode and expected-mapping-mode, tti-style (ITU-T-G709 default, or proprietary), tim-monitor (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tx-tti and expected-tti, loopback-mode (none, facility, terminal; default none) and the test-signal attributes. Example: set stm-1-5-T9.2 tx-mapping-mode BMP.

The trib-ptp attribute tributary-disable-action defines what the network element does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed, either shutting off the laser or inserting a replacement signal. Values are laser-shut-off (the default), none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais and send-nos (1830 GX G30 only). tributary-disable-holdoff-timer delays the client shutdown or replacement signal at egress, uint16 range 0..10000 milliseconds, default 0 meaning holdoff is disabled; it applies only when the TDA action is Laser-turnoff. Related switches: near-end-tda (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tda-degrade-mode for BERSD-ODU triggering ALS (default disabled) and forward-defect-trigger (true/false, default true). Example: set trib-ptp-1-5-T2 tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off.

Create with 'add xcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [payload-type <value>] [direction <value>] [label <value>] [circuit-id-suffix <value>]' in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode; source and destination are instance IDs. direction only accepts two-way, which is also the default. Examples: add xcon-11 source odu-1-1-3-ODU4 destination odu-1-1-1-ODU4-1; add xcon-1 source ethernet-1-4-T1 destination odu-1-4-T1-1-ODUni-1. protection-type is a show-only attribute representing the protection the XCON has, with values y-cable, snc-n, snc-i and unprotected, defaulting to unprotected. Other read-back attributes include type (add, drop, add-drop, express), payload-treatment, network-mapping, circuit-id and managed-by (user by default; only user created XCONs can be user deleted). 'set xcon-<name>' can only change label and circuit-id-suffix.

An L2-bridge is identified by bridge-name, a string of length 0..64 used in the instance name L2-bridge-<bridge-name>. Only set and show are supported, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode: 'set L2-bridge-<bridge-name> [chassis-name <value>] [description <value>]' and 'show L2-bridge-<bridge-name> [chassis-name] [description]'. There are just two configurable attributes: chassis-name, a leafref giving the chassis associated with this L2 bridge, and description, a string of length 0..255 describing the bridge and its intended purpose. Neither has a default.

Use the clear app command: 'clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value>'. It clears third party apps and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. app-name identifies the third party app to remove. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation, so omit it if you want the confirmation prompt. The guide lists no other parameters for this command.

Use 'appctl [app-name=]<value> [command=]<value> [[target=]<value>] [[parameters=]<value>[,<value>]*]' in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode. app-name is a leafref to the configured third-party-app app-name. command takes restart (restarts the third party application), netls (shows the list of subnet networks used by the containers) or exec (executes a third party application operation given in parameters). target is the scope: either the string system or a chassis/card AID, and it defaults to system. parameters is an optional string list with max-elements 50, applicable when command is restart or exec. None of app-name or command has a default.
